_meta.purpose: Per-condition strengths (blue, left) and weaknesses (red, right) as circles for abstract gradient visualization.
_meta.size_scale: 0.0 to 1.0, relative magnitude within this dataset only — not a clinical or statistical scale.

size_basis.measured: Derived from a reported effect size or percentage in the source text.
size_basis.described: No effect size given — sized from qualitative language (e.g. 'significant', 'reliable', 'broad', 'small').
size_basis.none_found: Source explicitly states no reliable strength exists for this domain.

_meta.source: user-provided literature summary, see references in original doc

strengths.label: Visuospatial perception
strengths.note: Relative strength vs. neurotypical controls (Kuo & Eack, 2020).

weaknesses.label: Working memory
weaknesses.note: 'Significantly smaller impairments' than other neurodevelopmental conditions, but present.

conditions.label: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder

weaknesses.label: Response inhibition
weaknesses.note: Significant executive function impairment (Bhattacharya et al., 2023).

conditions.notes: Source explicitly states meta-analytic literature does not establish a cognitive strength for OCD; 'hyper-focus' claims are anecdotal.

conditions.label: Bipolar Disorder

strengths.label: Divergent thinking / creative potential
strengths.note: Meta-analytic effect size d=0.11 — statistically significant but very small (Forthmann et al., 2023).

weaknesses.label: Sustained attention
weaknesses.note: Broad deficit, often persists even in stable (euthymic) phases.

weaknesses.label: Verbal memory
weaknesses.note: Broad deficit, persists in stable phases.

weaknesses.label: Executive functioning
weaknesses.note: Broad deficit, persists in stable phases.

conditions.notes: Creativity link follows an inverted-U: mild traits may help, severe episodes impair. Unaffected relatives outperform patients on creativity/success but that's a separate population, not included here.

strengths.label: Task accuracy (performance effectiveness)
strengths.note: Outperform healthy peers in accuracy on executive function tasks — but caveat: this is compensatory, not enhancement (Attentional Control Theory).
